questions.question: Why is it recommended NOT to use java.util.Date in new code?
options: It is slower than java.time
It is mutable, unsafe under concurrency, and has design problems (months start at 0)
It is deprecated and was removed in Java 17
It only works with the Gregorian calendar
explanations: Speed is not the main problem.
Correct. Date is mutable (not thread-safe), months start at 0, it mixes date and time, and it has a confusing API.
Date has not been removed; it is still available for compatibility.
Date works with the Gregorian calendar without restrictions.

questions.question: What is the difference between Period and Duration in java.time?
options: There is no difference, they are interchangeable
Period represents years/months/days, Duration represents hours/minutes/seconds
Period is for dates, Duration is for strings
Duration only works with LocalDate, Period with LocalTime
explanations: They are different classes with different purposes.
Correct. Period measures time in calendar units (years, months, days), while Duration measures time in precise clock units (hours, minutes, seconds, nanoseconds).
Both represent time intervals, not strings.
Period works with LocalDate and Duration with LocalTime, but the distinction is broader.

questions.question: How do you calculate the difference between two dates in java.time?
options: date1.diff(date2)
Period.between(date1, date2)
date1 - date2
Date.difference(date1, date2)
explanations: diff() does not exist as a method on LocalDate.
Correct. Period.between(date1, date2) returns a Period object with the difference in years, months, and days between both dates.
You cannot use the - operator directly with dates in Java.
Date.difference() does not exist.

questions.question: What does ZonedDateTime represent in java.time?
options: A date without a time zone
A date and time with a full time zone (offset and system zone)
A world time zone
A date in UTC format only
explanations: ZonedDateTime does include a time zone.
Correct. ZonedDateTime combines date, time, and time zone, including the UTC offset and the system zone (such as America/Mexico_City).
ZonedDateTime is a combination of date/time/zone, not just a zone.
ZonedDateTime supports any time zone, not only UTC.

questions.question: How do you convert a String with a date format to LocalDate?
options: LocalDate.toDate("2024-01-15")
LocalDate.parse("2024-01-15")
new LocalDate("2024-01-15")
LocalDate.fromString("2024-01-15")
explanations: toDate() is not a LocalDate method.
Correct. LocalDate.parse() converts a String in ISO-8601 format (yyyy-MM-dd) to a LocalDate object.
LocalDate does not have a constructor that takes a String.
fromString() is not a LocalDate method.
